### The reformulation (Type A, both directions proved here)

Fix 1 ≤ k ≤ n−1 and let F = n(n−1)⋯(n−k+1). Define

  Q(n,k) = max{ p prime : p > k, p ∣ F }  (and Q = 1 if the set is empty).

**Claim: P(C(n,k)) > k ⟺ Q(n,k) > k, and whenever Q(n,k) > k, P(C(n,k)) = Q(n,k).**

*Direction 1 (p>k ∣ F ⟹ p ∣ C(n,k)).* A prime p > k divides exactly one factor n−i, 0 ≤ i ≤ k−1. Then n ≡ i (mod p) with 0 ≤ i < k < p. Add k and n−k in base p (Kummer): units digits are k and (i−k mod p) = p−(k−i); their sum is p+i ≥ p, so there is at least one carry, hence by Kummer p ∣ C(n,k).

*Direction 2 (p>k ∣ C(n,k) ⟹ p ∣ F).* Trivial: C(n,k) = F/k!, and p > k means p ∤ k!, so p ∣ F. ∎
